# Phase Three — Final Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos is beyond every panel yet gives each panel permission to appear;
Awtsmoos.com should reveal context when sought, while source and answer remain near.

## Final Architecture: Quiet Threshold, Living Answer

The Sefarim page remains one route and keeps its existing search engine. The reconstruction changes only the visible hierarchy around that engine.

### Zone One — Compact Identity

The current 19rem hero becomes a shallow masthead. It keeps the Living Source Graph identity, the exact-source promise, and a restrained provenance sentence. The decorative orbital mark is removed from the dominant layout. Trust remains textual and specific rather than repeated through three badge pills.

### Zone Two — Search Task

The existing form remains intact. Its runtime Search Options disclosure keeps mode, strategy, lane, book, and corpus available. The query and Search button stay dominant. No controller or API behavior changes.

### Zone Three — Answer

Scope navigation and result status stay immediately above the result list. The workspace becomes a result-first reading surface instead of permanently reserving a right rail. Result provenance and coordinates remain untouched.

### Zone Four — Context On Demand

Wrap the existing discovery rail in a native `<details class="library-context">` element with a concise `<summary>` such as “Library context” plus an explanatory state line. The existing lane directory, browser history, and tip card keep their current IDs and behaviors inside this disclosure. No new JavaScript is required.

Desktop may present the opened context as a compact three-column grid. Mobile presents the opened context as a one-column stack. Closed is the calm default.

## Responsive Doctrine

- Wide/tall desktop: search form may remain sticky beneath the shared shell.
- Short-height desktop: search form returns to normal flow.
- Tablet: result-first single column; scope nav can scroll if necessary.
- Phone: compact identity, one-column form/results, native context disclosure, no 86vw context carousel.
- Extra narrow: preserve current safe-area and result-card safeguards from untouched `mobile.css`.

## Accessibility Doctrine

- Native form, labels, details, summary, buttons, and links remain native.
- Existing IDs and skip target remain unchanged.
- No hidden controls become focusable off-canvas.
- Focus-visible styling survives.
- Context disclosure gives keyboard and screen-reader users the same progressive access as pointer users.

## Visual Doctrine

- One cyan action accent rather than cyan borders around every block.
- Fewer bordered boxes.
- Smaller identity typography.
- Quiet tertiary metadata.
- Results receive the widest and most stable reading region.
- No extra gradients, assets, animation systems, fonts, or dependencies.

## Concurrency Doctrine

This wave touches only `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/**`, which was clean when ownership was checked. Immediately before writing, scoped Git status must be refreshed. If another agent has entered this subtree, production mutation stops and moves to another clean target.

## Post-Draft Verification

Only after the source draft exists: read back all touched files, run existing Sefarim contracts, load the actual public route without `/geelooy`, exercise query/search/context/history/lane interactions, inspect console/network, and test desktop/tablet/430px/short-height geometry.

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the exact execution file plan, refresh scoped Git status, then perform the first coherent full-file rewrite pass.
